messages:
ara: Heads-up — we're seeing a recurring pattern in ap-southeast1: paired local NVMe devices on a subset of GPU hosts hit synchronous thermal/IO spikes during nightly ephemeral cleanup windows, which collapses IOPS and blocks GPU attaches for ~30-90s.

linh: Oof. any SMART or kernel logs?

ara: quick slice from node gnode-apse1-42: ```
[ 23456.123456] nvme nvme0: thermal_throttle start
[ 23456.124000] blk_update_request: I/O error, dev nvme0n1, sector 4096
[ 23456.125000] nvme nvme1: thermal_throttle start
[ 23456.130000] nvme nvme0: queue depth 256 -> io_latency 180ms
```
Noticed both nvme0 & nvme1 spike at same time (they're on same board pair).

mike: That pattern sounds like thermal coupling between paired devices. Cleaner/janitor likely triggering concurrent deep-scrub on both devices. Can you `smartctl -a` them?

ara: ran quick SMART: ```
> smartctl -a /dev/nvme0n1
SMART overall-health self-assessment test result: PASSED
Temperature: 83 C
Power cycles: 1200
Media errors: 0
> smartctl -a /dev/nvme1n1
Temperature: 85 C
Power cycles: 1200
Media errors: 2 (retries)
```
Temps are high during the window. Media errors small but correlated with IOPS blips.

sara: Are these hosts on our cheaper thermal limit firmware? We had a batch with relaxed thermal headroom last quarter.

linh: Yes, those are the batch that shipped with the alternate cooling shroud. They're fine normally but we shouldn't stomp both drives simultaneously.

mike: Actionable: throttle janitor concurrency per-node and prefer single-device passes instead of simultaneous deep-scrub on both NVMe devices. Also consider staggering cleaner cron offsets across the pool.

ara: Proposed quick mitigation: roll an emergency config to set janitor.concurrency_per_node=1 and janitor.device_stagger=true for ap-southeast1 scrub jobs. Patch ready: ```yaml
jobs:
  scrub_ephemeral:
    concurrency_per_node: 1
    device_stagger: true
    window: "02:00-05:00"
```
Will push canary to 5% of nodes first. Thoughts?

sara: Do it. We should also add a temporary routing rule so new GPU allocs avoid the most affected hosts while canary lands.

linh: I'll open a small probe to reassign attach requests away from gnode-hotlist cluster via routing policy. That buys time.

mike: Cost tradeoff note: throttling janitor increases average scratch occupancy and delays cleanup, which raises risk of snapshot pressure and slightly higher storage costs. But that's favorable vs repeated GPU attach failures. Recommend throttle + stagger for 72h and monitor.

ara: Agreed. I'll run the rollout: ```bash
./infractl rollout-config --env ap-southeast1 --service janitor --patch patch.yaml --percent 5
```
Deploy-bot: rollout started for janitor in ap-southeast1 (5% canary) — id=rb-20260322-11

pagerduty-bot: Incident created: #INC-8421 "ap-southeast1 NVMe thermal coupling causing GPU attach failures" assigned to eng-oncall

sara: After canary: if stable, bump to 50% and update routing to gradually reintroduce hosts. Also schedule a targeted firmware review for that HW batch.

linh: I'll also add a heatmap to telemetry: correlate nvme temp, janitor job start time, and attach-fail counts so we can alert earlier next time. Sketch: `nvme.temp.avg(5m)`, `janitor.jobs.running`, `gpu.attach.fail.rate(1m)`.

ara: Quick check-in in 30m once canary finishes. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
